single.rationale: Delcath shows exceptional inflection from commercial-stage launch of HEPZATO, with revenue exploding from $2M to $85M (129% YoY growth) and turning operating cash flow positive ($22.5M) in FY2025. dropped.claim: Operating margin of 0.8% ($660,000 operating income on $85.2M revenue) is presented as merely 'razor-thin,' but the context is more alarming: R&D spending doubled from $13.9M in 2024 to $29.2M in 2025 as Phase 2 trials launched. If the company had maintained 2024 R&D levels, operating income would have been approximately $15.9M higher. The profitability is thus artificial and temporary—management is deliberately suppressing margins to fund trials with endpoints in 2027-2029, meaning multi-year losses are virtually guaranteed as R&D continues to scale.

dropped.claim: The thesis mentions Phase 2 trials in colorectal and breast cancer but understates the commercial risk: these are randomized controlled trials in third-line treatment populations (6,000-10,000 patients for colorectal, 7,000 for breast cancer annually in the US), with primary endpoint hepatic progression-free survival (hPFS) reading out 2027-2028. However, overall survival (OS)—the endpoint most likely to drive reimbursement and adoption—is a secondary endpoint not expected until 2028-2029. Even successful hPFS results may not translate to commercial viability without OS benefit, potentially delaying revenue expansion by 4-5 years from present.
